newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers fall, rest of Europe expected to dip.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers fall, rest of Europe expected to dip.

text.p: ARA fuel oil bunkers lost $4/$5 a tonne as barge price support gave way, but bunkers in other areas held steady, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST traded in the range $110-$112 fob. Dealers said demand picked up in the afternoon as the fall of barge prices worked its way into the bunker market. In contrast, diesel and gas oil prices rose as IPE gas oil futures gained about $3 a tonne.
Hamburg 380 CST remained at $120 ex-wharf. A few small volumes propped up prices, but many expected prices to weaken in line with Rotterdam, dealers said.
Mediterranean prices were broadly unchanged from Friday's close. Business was slack in most parts, although ports in southern France registered reasonable interest.
"The buyers are again expecting price falls, so, of course, they don't buy," one trader said.
In Durban, supply again became a problem. Suppliers said fuel oil may not become readily available again until October. Fuel oil prices were accordingly strong.
